Throughout his life Shu spent more days on temple appointments and in retirement than in active office. While serving in the Ministry of Rites, he routinely handled memorials for the Three Departments. When a great fire ravaged Lin'an, Emperor Ningzong, responding to the calamity, avoided the main hall. The Secretariat submitted three memorials asking him to resume normal court, but permission was denied. Shu drafted the response, striving to uphold proper principle rather than flatter and compromise. Critics picked out his wording as slanderous of the sovereign, but the court knew he meant no harm, and the edict recalling him to office included the phrase "clear wind and lofty integrity."
起復制詞 is the edict restoring Tang Shu to office, not the emperor resuming court.

In his life the days Shu spent on temple appointments and in retirement were more than those in official promotion; when he was in the Ministry of Rites section, by precedent he handled memorials for the Three Departments. When a great fire broke out in Lin'an, Emperor Ningzong met with disaster and avoided the main hall; the Secretariat submitted three memorials requesting resumption, but this was not granted. Shu drafted the wording, striving to uphold the larger principles and not to flatter and bend; critics seized upon his language as involving slander of the sovereign, yet the court in fact knew he had no other intent, and so the edict text for resumption contained the phrase "clear wind and lofty integrity."

unresolvedReferences.description: The heading names five biographies. Mou Zicai, Zhu Pisun, and Ouyang Shoudao appear only here in this stretch and are bounded by the external end of Song.
Zhu Xi's summons has no year in the chapter; 1194 is external. The chief minister in power in s0006 is not named and is not identified.
Tang Shu's death has no year.
起復 is Tang Shu's recall; repaired. The Lin'an fire is not dated here.
先帝 and 聖母 are unnamed titles (late emperor, empress dowager) and are not made people.

臨御八年 implies about 1231 by external count from Lizong's 1224 accession, while the narrative year is Shaoding 3 (1230). The discrepancy is noted, and this unit is not used as dating evidence. The 丞相 is not named.
莊文府 is an institution, disposed as office, not the prince himself.
帝 is not named; Lizong is an external identification.
充國 is Zhao Chongguo by identification; the surname is not in the Chinese. The frontier commander is not named.
Yunliang was one year old in the Chunhua era (external 990-994). The age is not turned into a birth year. The aunt is unnamed.
内外艱 is the deaths of mother and father; each has a descriptive record. Chengdu's fall is not dated in the chapter.
Chancellorship years for Li Zongmian, Shi Songzhi, Zheng Qingzhi, Xie Fangshu, and Wu Qian are external.
s0076 writes 寀 where s0073 and s0075 write 宷 for Zheng Shen. Both are kept as written.
作書與孔光、張禹 is a letter styled after letters to Han ministers. Kong Guang and Zhang Yu are allusions only.
The chief counselor who merged the lectures is not named.
起居郎 is repaired to Diarist.
潼遂 is Tong and Sui, repaired.
No year is stated in this stretch. All dates are external, bounded 1251-1259.
The chief counselor is not named.
The Tian and Yang families are collective and not made people.
皇子 is not named and is not identified; crown prince is repaired to imperial son.
謝堂等 names only Xie Tang among the others.
七十萬緡 is repaired to seven hundred thousand.
妃子 is the Tang consort (by identification Yang Guifei) and is not named; she is not made a person.
The idiomatic and literal add zither, guests, and cash that the Chinese does not have; repaired.
實章閣 may be a variant of 寶章閣; kept as written. 潛黨 is Wu Qian's faction by identification.
開慶 is Kaiqing, external AD 1259.
The comet and public fields memorial is placed in 1264 by external chronology.
Zicai's death has no year. 後二人 are two unnamed descendants, kept as a counted summary.
事親 covers his parents generally. The younger brother is unnamed and has his own record as Fang's father.
The work list reads 口義故事四尚易編、春秋輪輻子》獻, with an unmatched closing bracket; it is kept as written and not split into invented titles.
The commissioners' dates are external.
The Chinese gives no number ten and ends with a clause the English dropped; repaired. The six scholars are collective.
太子 is identified with Duzong because s0208 says Duzong valued their old teaching relationship; strongly inferred.
春秋髙 means advanced in age, not the Spring and Autumn Annals.
田里歡聲 is repaired from rising rent.
巽 is his original name, kept for sacrifices.
The district magistrate is not named and is not made a person.
陳日照 reads Chen Rizhao; the English Riyao is repaired. The abdication year 1258 is external. The king's son is unnamed.
The 古公 passage is repaired; the Old Duke is cited only.
史贊 is the historian's appraisal; the Great General (cited by allusion, and by analogy Lü Wende) is not made a separate person.
上 here is the reigning emperor after 1267, by external chronology Duzong; not named, not made a person.
Shoudao's death has no year.
Yan is explicitly the sister-in-law's son. Jun's parentage is inferred from 二子 and is marked strongly inferred.
The worthy prefect of Ji is not named.
